mt: 'ELMCIP ELECTRONIC LITERATURE KNOWLEDGE BASE' ON THE OVERVIEW — THE FROZEN ARCHIVE AT ITS GRAIN AND ITS CLOSING MONTH; ITS COUNTS GIVEN AS THOUSANDS; NO RECORD NAMED, TAROKO GORGE AND THE 1952 GENERATOR AMONG THEM
d: THE KNOWLEDGE BASE, SIGNED OUT, 2026-11-01: 'The ELMCIP Electronic Literature Knowledge Base is a comprehensive, cross-referenced digital humanities research resource for electronic literature, preserved as a frozen archive on the ELMCIP Official Website.' Key details: status ('Frozen archive (active from June 2010 to October 2026; no longer open for new submissions or contributions)'); origin (Drupal 7, the University of Bergen group, 'the six-nation ELMCIP project (Electronic Literature as a Model of Creativity and Innovation in Practice, 2010–2013) led by Scott Rettberg'); content ('thousands of interconnected records'); legacy (the Digital Narrative Knowledge Base); a follow-up offer. Five cards: the ELMCIP Knowledge Base, www.elmcip.it, electronic book review, Arquivo Digital da PO.EX, a Facebook post of the Knowledge Base.
reading: The innocent reading first. Asked for the knowledge base, the Overview says what it is and that it is frozen, gives its dates, its makers and the project behind it, what kinds of record it holds and what succeeds it, and offers to help browse it.
findings: THE FROZEN ARCHIVE AT ITS GRAIN. 'Frozen archive (active from June 2010 to October 2026; no longer open for new submissions or contributions)'. The saved page: 'Electronic Literature Knowledge Base June 2010 – October 2026', 'now preserved as a frozen archive' and 'The archive remains available for browsing and searching, but is no longer open for new contributions or submissions.' The closing month the census row records, a month before the capture, is in the composition; the browsing and searching that remain are offered in its follow-up ('how to browse the frozen archive').

THE MAKERS AND THE PROJECT. 'Developed in Drupal 7 by the University of Bergen Electronic Literature Research Group as a core outcome of the six-nation ELMCIP project'. The page: 'It was developed in Drupal 7 by the University of Bergen Electronic Literature Research Group as an outcome of the ELMCIP project.' The expansion of the acronym, 'six-nation', '2010–2013' and 'led by Scott Rettberg' are on no saved source; on the saved page Rettberg appears as an author of records. The community the page credits, 'built through the active participation of a community of international researchers and writers', and its licence, 'Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International', are not carried.

THE COUNTS AS THOUSANDS. 'Houses thousands of interconnected records covering authors, creative works, critical writing, platforms, events, organizations, publishers, and teaching resources.' The page: '17,073 published records preserved.', with 'Creative Works 4,011 records', 'Critical Writing 5,060 records', 'Authors 4,826 records'. The record types agree with the page's list; 'Databases and Archives 78 records' and 'Research Collections 69 records', among them 'Bot-mimicry Bots!', are not carried.

NO RECORD NAMED. The census row reads ELMCIP for what its records hold under their authors' names: 'Taroko Gorge Nick Montfort 2009 text generator , poetry generator', 'M.U.C. Love Letter Generator Christopher Strachey 1952', 'Stochastische Texte Theo Lutz 1959'. The composition names no work and no author of a work; the procedural lineage the census row reads it as indexing, from a generator of 1952 to one of 2009, is not reached. The second card is a second domain under the name, www.elmcip.it, titled with the project's full name; the census row's address is elmcip.net.
analysis: The frozen knowledge base composed accurately, with its closing month of October 2026, its makers and its successor. Its counts become 'thousands', and none of its records, the generators the census row holds it for, is named.
per_note: Scott Rettberg and the University of Bergen group named; no identifier; the knowledge base's own page carded first.
